source.title: RF-GPT: Teaching AI to See the Wireless World
source.authors: Han Zou; Yu Tian; Bo-Hao Wang; Lina Bariah; S. Lasaulce; Chong-Wen Huang; M. Debbah

record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream benchmark performance for 3B and 7B models, which bears conceptually on V6, but it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study does not test held-out cross-entropy power laws, extrapolation from small pretraining runs, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture effects at fixed parameter count. Its relevant results are downstream benchmark scores for two model sizes; the RF-GPT models also receive RF-grounded fine-tuning. Other results, such as the input-resolution ablation, do not measure parameter-count scaling.
record.test_reason: This is an RF-spectrogram fine-tuning method paper. Its only size-related results compare its own two fine-tuned variants (RF-GPT-3B vs 7B, built on different Qwen2.5-VL checkpoints) and two untuned instruct baselines, on downstream RF benchmarks. It fits no pretraining loss, scaling curve, extrapolation or compute allocation. Two backbone sizes cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or with loss. The size comparison is a side observation about the authors' own method variants, not a test of any version, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that RF-grounded instruction tuning turns general VLMs, which show very limited RF understanding, into strong multi-task RF models that are competitive with CNN/Transformer baselines. In passing they say the 7B variant improves on 3B, indicating larger models extract richer structure. They draw no scaling-law conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: This is an RF understanding study using synthetic RF scenes, spectrogram inputs, and supervised instruction fine-tuning; it does not run a language-model pretraining scaling-law or compute-allocation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream results vary by benchmark and task difficulty; the paper reports that RF-GPT-7B is similar or slightly better than RF-GPT-3B on WBOD-Easy and WBOD-Medium, and similar or improved on most NRIE tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: RF-fine-tuned 7B scores at or above RF-fine-tuned 3B on every benchmark: WBMC, WBOD, WTR, WNUC, NRIE, and the unseen-task Q1/Q3. Untuned 3B and 7B instruct models are equal at near-chance levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After domain-specific fine-tuning, a larger backbone of the same family scores higher on downstream tasks (two-point comparison, no predictability shown).

record.code_released: no; the paper says benchmark materials are planned for release, while generator, training-pipeline, and instruction-synthesis code are not part of the public release
record.problems: The size comparison has only two model sizes and no uncertainty estimates. The models are RF-grounded and fine-tuned, so the comparisons do not establish pretraining-loss scaling or a general downstream scaling law.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark values for general-purpose models and fine-grained per-class or per-attribute values were not extracted where the text did not provide a clearly paired size comparison. The image-resolution ablation changes resolution rather than parameter count and does not bear on V6.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured or fitted.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in the RF/spectrogram or fine-tuning regime.
Only two fine-tuned sizes on different backbones; no curve, no predictability test, no loss-performance relation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V6 labels are overturned: the study is not a test because it offers only two own-method sizes on different pretrained checkpoints with no loss or predictability analysis. Other size contrasts, such as UTB Table VIII (7B vs 3B on Q1 62.8/49.6 and Q3 100/58), were not extracted, but they bear on no version. Internal inconsistency: WTR 7B joint accuracy is 99.64% in the text and Fig. 8 but 99.78% in the confusion-matrix text.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run losses from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations across compute budgets.
Architecture variation at fixed parameter count and its effect on loss.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study compares only two model sizes and does not establish a scaling curve or predictability; it reports no relation between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices.

relation.reason: The study comments qualitatively on larger models extracting richer RF structure; it neither tests nor uses the specified scaling-law claims.

tranche.reason: RF instruction-tuning benchmarks compare two model sizes and design choices without fitting or testing a scaling law, extrapolation, compute allocation, or predictable downstream relationship.

source_check.notes: All listed rows appropriately remain cannot_determine with versions none. Exact WBOD values are available in Fig. 7; the conflicting WTR accuracies are an internal source inconsistency.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RF-GPT-3B and RF-GPT-7B on the reported RF benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The larger RF-GPT model scores higher on the explicitly paired WBMC levels, WBOD-Hard, WTR, and WNUC, and is described as similar or better on most NRIE tasks (r1-r6, r11-r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Two-size comparisons and off-the-shelf Qwen2.5-VL controls
reader_labels.reason: Only two sizes are compared, with no scaling curve or loss-based prediction; the larger untuned Qwen2.5-VL model scores lower on WTR and WNUC (r19-r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported 7B advantage is described only as similar or slightly better on WBOD-Easy/Medium and similar or improved on most NRIE tasks, without exact paired values in the text (r7-r10, r17-r18).
